title: Plenty of Rooms
youtube_title: She moved into a CEO's house — and brought her ex's mother
logline: Nora moves into the concrete Ashford house on the hill and brings Peg. The house rules are as cold as the contract, Peg rejects every one, and on the first night the grief Nora has held for three months finally breaks.
hook: In the car up the hill, Theo glances at his tablet, screen away from us: “Ms. Vale's post.” “Deleted three minutes ago.” Out the window, a grey concrete house juts from the hillside — one whole wall, two windows.
mid_hook: Elias: “Plenty of rooms.” He hands her a key and a card, and reads it out himself: “Separate rooms.” “Stay out of the study.” “Don't wait on dinner.” Peg snatches it and rereads the last one: “Number three?” She smacks it on the table. “No.”
extra_hooks: Peg opens the double-door fridge: bottled water and coffee beans. “You rich people live on takeout?” Theo, voice-over, deadpan: “Mrs. Ashford Observation Log.” “Day one.” “No smile.”
conflict: Nora has to live in a stranger's house until the day Grant is sentenced. The house rules are as cold as the contract, and Peg means to cook in a kitchen nobody has ever used.
turn: That first night, unpacking, Nora finds the baby's half-knitted hat on her pillow — Peg put it back. She slides down the concrete wall clutching it and sobs out loud. In the hall, Peg's hand stops on the doorknob; she doesn't go in, and cries alone. The next night the long table nobody uses holds a full dinner. Peg has made it a home.

cliffhanger.text: Next night, nine o'clock. Elias walks in to a full table and three place settings. Peg stands in front of the study door, arms folded: “Sit.” “Eat.”
cliffhanger.question: Will Elias sit down to eat?

spectacle: A grey board-formed concrete house set into the hillside, one wall with only two windows; at night the only lights on are the kitchen and one guest room where someone is crying.
glamour_shot: Elias slips off his coat in the entry — black turtleneck, thin-framed glasses — sees the full table and stops a beat; behind the lenses, for the first time, he looks unsure.
general_payoffs: Nora and Peg each have their own room and key
Peg gives back the baby's hat and starts cooking in the Ashford house
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (entry, guest rooms, kitchen, long dining table, study door)

title: Front Row, Center
youtube_title: Her ex's launch invite came to her new home. Front row
logline: Elias sits down at Peg's table. The same night, Whitlock Home's launch invitation arrives at the Ashford house, Nora's seat is front row center, and a phone call tells her Grant has known where she is all along.
hook: Elias looks at Peg for three seconds, takes off his jacket and sits, left hand under the table. He eats every bite. Peg: “Well?” Elias: “…Acceptable.” Peg, to Nora: “That means good.”
mid_hook: Theo sets a gold-foil envelope on the table and reads it: “For Mr. and Mrs. Ashford.” He slides out her seat card: “Front row, center.” Nora looks a long time: “He wants to see what I wear to cry.”
conflict: Grant has put her front row center so every camera catches the ex-wife “divorced at noon, married to a billionaire by five.” Staying home looks like running. Going looks like walking into it.
turn: Nora reads the invitation as a taunt — until she turns it over and reads the last line aloud: “Forever No. 1.” She stops. “Shown for the first time.” The vase she blew at twenty-five is going on his stage.

cliffhanger.text: Late that night her phone rings. Sienna: “Mrs. Ashford.” “Nice house.” “Concrete's cold, huh?” Grant laughs in the background. Nora looks down at the phone he gave her — still on his family plan.
cliffhanger.question: Is he tracking her phone?

spectacle: Steam rises off a full dinner on the long concrete table; beside it a gold-foil envelope throws back the ceiling light like a slab of cold metal (only the gold glare and hands, no readable text).
glamour_shot: Nora, shoulder-length hair, plain cream sweater, reads the invitation at the far end of the long table; the overhead light drops a small shadow of lashes on her cheek.
general_payoffs: Elias sits at Peg's table and finishes a full plate
The back of the invitation tells her Forever No. 1 will be on stage

title: Factory-Made, No Name
youtube_title: His store says he designed her vase. She flips every one
logline: Nora pulls the SIM from the phone Grant gave her and goes to see Forever at Whitlock Home's flagship store, afraid the factory copied the one thing that could prove the vase is hers.
hook: She pops the SIM out of Grant's phone and drops it face down in a drawer: “He always knew where I was.” Next day she opens a line with her own money. Peg writes and reads aloud: “Phone line.” “Thirty.”
mid_hook: In the flagship window, a huge poster of Grant cradling a white vase. The clerk recites: “Forever No. 1. First showing.” “Mr. Whitlock designed it himself.” Nora: “Did he.”
conflict: If the factory molded Forever from No. 1, base and all, the bubbles are in every vase on the shelf — and her proof is worth nothing. Hundreds of identical Forevers wait to be checked.
turn: She turns them over one by one under the case light, each one tighter than the last: “If they copied the base, I've got nothing.” The clerk: “Ma'am, please don't handle the merchandise.” Nora: “I made the first one.” Two customers turn. The last base is blank like all the rest. The factory never copied it. Only No. 1 holds what she put there.

cliffhanger.text: Back at the Ashford house she turns the invitation “No. 1” side up and slides it to Peg: “There's something inside No. 1.” “He's never seen it.”
cliffhanger.question: What's hidden inside No. 1?

spectacle: On the brightest wall of the flagship store, hundreds of identical Forever vases stand in rows; by the door a brass builder's plaque catches the light as the clerk mentions, “Ashford built this place.”
glamour_shot: She holds a factory Forever upside down to the case light, hair tucked behind her ear, squinting at the base — for a second she's back at the furnace.
general_payoffs: She pays for her own phone line and cuts off Grant's tracking
The factory never copied the base: only No. 1 holds her bubbles

title: You're the One on Stage
youtube_title: He left a grey gown at her door: “You're the one on stage.”
logline: Elias leaves a misty-grey gown for the launch and says he'll be in the audience. It fits exactly. In front of the mirror, Nora realizes how close she would have been to her due date — and comes apart.
hook: At the study door, Elias hands her a long box with his right hand: “For Thursday.” Inside: a misty-grey gown. “You're the one on stage.” “I'll be in the audience.” He shuts the study door.
mid_hook: At the mirror the gown fits. Misty grey — her color at nineteen. Her hand drifts to her flat stomach and stops. “I'd be due next month.” She folds to the floor, sobbing. Peg runs in, kneels, holds her: “I know.” “I know.”
extra_hooks: Still on the floor, Peg wipes her own eyes and opens the ledger, reading as she writes: “One gown.” “Owed to Ashford.” Nora laughs through the tears: “I'll pay for the dress.” Peg: “You will.”
conflict: Nora wants to go up there in her own clothes, on her own two hands. She can't afford a decent dress, anything he gives her can be called bought — and the mirror shows her the body that should be eight months along.
turn: She assumed he was just opening a door, per clause two. But the gown fits like she was measured, in a color even she had nearly forgotten — and putting it on is the first time since the hospital she lets herself count the months.

cliffhanger.text: She runs to the study door holding up her hem: “How did you know I love this color?” The door is open, the room empty. Theo leans over the banister: “He says he didn't.”
cliffhanger.question: How did he know about grey?

spectacle: At the end of the concrete hallway stands a floor-length mirror; a misty-grey gown pools on the cold floor where two women hold each other.
glamour_shot: In the misty-grey gown at the mirror — shoulder-length hair, a clean neckline — her own reflection stops her, tear-streaked, like someone she hasn't seen in years.
general_payoffs: She has a gown for the stage, logged as a debt in Peg's ledger
She grieves the due date out loud, and Peg grieves with her
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (study door, hallway, floor-length mirror)

title: Cease and Desist
youtube_title: Her ex's lawyer warned her off. She picked up the gown
logline: The size came from Peg. But three days before the launch, Leonard Fisk sends a cease-and-desist letter warning her off the stage. Dana gives her the law straight, and leaves the choice to her.
hook: Peg leans out of the kitchen: “The size was me.” “I was your mother-in-law six years.” She points at Theo: “He asked.” Theo pushes up his glasses: “The boss told me to.”
mid_hook: Certified mail from Leonard Fisk's office. Nora reads two pieces aloud: “Disrupt the event.” “Damage any exhibit.” Peg translates from the stove: “Touch anything, they sue.”
extra_hooks: Dana on speaker: “Attending isn't a crime.” “Touch nothing bare-handed.” “The rest is your call.” On the stairs, Elias stands and looks once. He doesn't come down.
conflict: Fisk strikes first: touch anything on that stage and it's disruption and damage. Dana tells her what the law allows; Elias, holding to clause two, won't tell her to go or stay. The choice is hers alone.
turn: Nora reads the letter as “stay home.” On the second read she gets it: Fisk isn't afraid she'll show up. He's afraid she'll touch No. 1. They don't know what's in it — but they're scared she does.

cliffhanger.text: Three things side by side on the long table: the letter, the invitation, the grey gown. She looks a long time, folds the letter under the others, and picks up the gown.
cliffhanger.question: Will she still take the stage?

spectacle: A pendant light over the concrete table: the cease-and-desist letter, the gold-foil invitation and a folded grey gown in a row, like three cards she has to pick from.
glamour_shot: Reading the letter, her hair falls along her cheek; at the words “damage any exhibit,” the corner of her mouth moves, barely.
general_payoffs: The gown size came from Peg; nobody answers about the color
She decides to go to the launch

title: Every Woman Who Keeps a Home
youtube_title: Her ex sat her front row, then swung the spotlight onto her
logline: Nora walks into the Forever launch in the grey gown, seated alone in front of every camera. On stage, Grant calls her vase a tribute to women who keep a home — then uses the baby she lost as a line in his speech.
hook: At the entrance Theo reads the seat cards: “Mrs. Ashford, front row, center.” “Mr. Ashford, second row, far end.” “They split you up.” She takes her seat alone. White flashes pulse across her face, shutters clattering.
mid_hook: Sienna takes the stage, flipping cue cards with her left hand: “It started with my grandmother's vase.” Center stage, under a glass dome, sits a vase Nora knows by heart — its lip just slightly crooked.
extra_hooks: At the far end of the front row a stocky man flipping a poker chip laughs out loud: “Grant, that vase outsells my condos!” Grant gives him a small bow from the stage.
conflict: Grant split the couple's seats so every lens finds the remarried ex-wife alone in the front row. Nora has to find a way to speak on a stage that isn't hers.
turn: She thought she'd just sit there and get photographed. But under that glass dome is the No. 1 she blew at twenty-five — that slight tilt at the lip is her own.

cliffhanger.text: Grant walks downstage with the mic, voice soft: “My ex-wife is here tonight.” “She lost our baby this spring.” “Please, be kind to her.” The spotlight swings onto her face. Her tears spill. She doesn't look down.
cliffhanger.question: Will she lower her eyes?

glamour_shot: The spotlight finds her — grey gown, shoulder-length hair, tears running. Everyone waits for her to look down. She slowly lifts her chin.

title: Lights Out
youtube_title: Her ex put her in the spotlight. She asked for the dark
logline: Grant wants the spotlight to make her look down. Nora walks into it and onto the stage, pulls on gloves, and asks the lighting tech for darkness.
hook: She stands up in the spotlight — and walks toward the stage, not the exit. A guard grabs for her arm. Far end of the second row, Elias stands: “She's a guest.” The guard knows him: “Mr. Ashford.” His hand drops. Elias sits back down.
mid_hook: At the glass dome she pulls on the white cotton gloves by the plinth and looks up at the lighting booth: “Kill the house lights.” “Leave the plinth on.”
extra_hooks: Grant laughs into the mic: “My ex-wife is a little emotional—” She doesn't turn around: “Give me two minutes.” “Then it's your mic.”
conflict: She has to show the room what's inside that vase before security walks her off — without damaging a single exhibit, with Fisk's letter still in her clutch.
turn: The crowd expects her to grab the mic and make a scene. She asks for the lights off instead. She doesn't want the room to hear her yet. She wants it to see.

cliffhanger.text: Ray the lighting tech hesitates one second, then cuts the house lights. The room goes black. Only the plinth's light box glows. She lifts No. 1 out of the dome and sets it upside down on the light.
cliffhanger.question: What's in the base of No. 1?

spectacle: The whole launch hall drops into darkness at once; only a glowing light box on the plinth remains, lighting a pair of white-gloved hands from below.
glamour_shot: In white gloves she bends over the glowing plinth in the black room, the grey hem pooled on the stage; light from below carves her face out of the dark.
general_payoffs: She takes the stage and gets her hands on her own No. 1
Elias says three words, and security doesn't touch her again

title: There's a Name Inside
youtube_title: She turned the vase over on his stage. It held her name
logline: In the dark, Nora sends light up through the base of No. 1. A line of tiny bubbles spells her initials — a trick Walter Pell taught her — and Sienna's grandmother story falls apart in front of everyone.
hook: Light climbs through the base of No. 1. A line of tiny bubbles glows, then settles into two letters: N.Q. (bubble letters composited in post). Nora: “My initials.” A breath. “My wedding day.”
mid_hook: She faces the room: “There's a name inside this vase.” Flashback: nineteen, at the furnace, Walter Pell's hands over hers on the blowpipe: “Whatever you make,” “leave your name inside.” Back on stage, her voice catches a beat before she goes on.
extra_hooks: She turns to Sienna: “Your grandmother's vase?” “I blew it at twenty-five.” Sienna's cue cards slip from her left hand and scatter. Front row, Victor Crane's chip stops between his fingers. He laughs out loud: “Grant, you didn't know?”
conflict: Nora needs everyone to see, at a glance, who made Forever. Grant still holds the mic, and the room is full of press he invited.
turn: The crowd thinks Forever was just stolen credit. But bubbles like these can only be set while the glass is being blown. No factory vase has them — only the one she made by hand. Grant kept it on a shelf for six years and never noticed.

cliffhanger.text: She sets the vase back under the dome and looks at Grant, voice shaking: “Six years,” “and you never once turned it over.” Tears fall; she keeps her eyes on him. Grant takes the mic from the host, smile back in place: “My ex-wife—”
cliffhanger.question: How will Grant spin this?

spectacle: In the dark hall the big screen shows only a row of glowing points rising like stars; in the front row, three or four phones lift, their screens the only other light.
glamour_shot: Light through the base scatters points of brightness across her wet cheek and lashes; she looks out at the room and doesn't wipe her face.
general_payoffs: The whole room sees the bubbles: N.Q., her initials, set on her wedding day
She says it in public: Forever was her wedding gift, blown at twenty-five, not Sienna's grandmother's

title: Don't You Dare
youtube_title: He told the press she hadn't recovered. She took the mic
logline: Grant tries to paint her as an unstable ex-wife who hasn't gotten over their baby. Nora takes the mic and shouts him down, the press turns on him, and his biggest backer walks out.
hook: Grant, into the mic: “My ex-wife hasn't quite recovered.” “From losing our—” Nora snatches the host's mic: “Don't you dare talk about my baby.” Silence. Then, low: “I made that vase.” “For you.”
mid_hook: Front row, Lyle Becker raises his hand: “Then why isn't her name on the label?” Victor Crane stands, buttons his jacket, and passes the stage: “Call me when this is cleaned up.” Grant's smile slips for the first time.
extra_hooks: On the way out, a voice message from Dana plays: “You wore gloves.” “You held your own name.” “That letter's got nothing.”
conflict: Grant wants the bubbles to be a marriage keepsake and Nora to be a grieving, unstable ex. She needs this to stay about who made the vase — without accusing him of the pills on a stage where Fisk's letter is waiting.
turn: Grant thought the press was his. Then she said “my baby” at full volume and the room went quiet. A mic swings to Elias: “Did you set this up?” He stays seated: “She's the one on stage.” “I'm in the audience.” The questions turn to Grant.

cliffhanger.text: She steps off the stage. In the corridor, Grant's driver Cole, white gloves, blocks her way: “Mr. Whitlock's backstage.” “He has something to show you.” Down the corridor, a light flickers once.
cliffhanger.question: What's he got backstage?

glamour_shot: Elias in the second row — charcoal suit, thin-framed glasses — ringed by microphones and still seated, lifts his eyes once to her on stage.
general_payoffs: She answers Grant in public, in her own voice, and the press asks about the name on the label

title: Then Prove It
youtube_title: He showed her a signature she never signed: “Prove it.”
logline: Backstage, Grant produces a transfer of the Forever design rights to his company, signed before the wedding. Even if the property agreement falls, Forever stays his. Nora holds the copies to the light — and Peg, at full volume, tells her son what she heard.
hook: Backstage corridor. Grant hands her a copy, smiling warmly: “You signed the rights to the company before the wedding.” “Even if your agreement falls,” “Forever was the company's first.” Nora: “That's not my signature.” Grant: “Then prove it.”
mid_hook: She lays the transfer copy over her property-agreement copy and holds both up to the corridor lamp. The two signatures' shadows sit exactly on top of each other. “Nobody signs the same twice.”
extra_hooks: Grant leans in: “You couldn't keep our baby.” “You won't keep this either.” The stage door bangs open — Peg, from the car, in front of stagehands and Lyle's raised phone: “That was my grandbaby!” “I heard every word up there.” “I'm ashamed you're mine.”
conflict: The bubbles prove Nora made Forever; the transfer says she gave the rights to the company before the wedding, so even a forged property agreement wouldn't win them back. She says she never signed it. Grant: who's a judge going to believe?
turn: She thought she'd won tonight, but Grant had the next page ready. Still, the corridor lamp shows her what a glass designer sees: two signatures that overlap perfectly were traced, not signed. And Grant's own mother has just shamed him where the press can hear.

cliffhanger.text: Grant straightens his cuffs and walks past his mother without a word. At the end of the corridor, Elias stands waiting, left hand in his pocket, and doesn't take a step. Theo: “Boss, aren't you going over?” Elias: “Clause two.”
cliffhanger.question: How does she prove it's fake?

spectacle: A long backstage corridor with only a few lights on; two photocopies held up to one lamp, their ink shadows merging into one, and at the far end a figure who doesn't move.
glamour_shot: The corridor's last light falls on Elias — charcoal suit, straight shoulders, left hand in his pocket. He watches her and doesn't take a step.
general_payoffs: She proves to herself the two signatures overlap exactly: traced, not signed
Peg denounces Grant in front of the crew and the press
